## Likely Cause of the Desk-Job Back Pain

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

The pattern fits **mechanical low back pain** from prolonged sitting, reduced movement, and likely muscle/tendon strain or stiffness around the spine and hips.
Because it is mild, improves with walking, and there are no neurologic symptoms or injury, this sounds **more like posture/load-related pain than a serious cause**.

## What It Most Likely Is

| Likely cause | Why it fits | What usually helps |
|---|---|---|
| Postural/mechanical strain | Worse after sitting, better with walking | Movement breaks, ergonomic changes |
| Tight hip flexors/hamstrings | Common with desk work and prolonged sitting | Stretching, walking, mobility work |
| Weak trunk/glute support | Can make sitting and bending feel worse | Gentle strengthening 3x/week |
| Irritated joints/discs without nerve involvement | Pain without numbness, fever, or injury | Activity modification, gradual return to normal movement |

## Red Flags That Need Medical Attention

Seek prompt medical care if any of these appear:

- New **numbness, tingling, or weakness** in a leg
- Pain that shoots below the knee and is getting worse
- **Loss of bladder or bowel control**
- **Saddle numbness**: numbness in the groin or inner thighs
- **Fever**, chills, or feeling unwell with back pain
- Back pain after a **fall, accident, or heavy lifting injury**
- History of **cancer**, IV drug use, immune suppression, or unexplained weight loss
- Pain that is **constant at rest**, severe at night, or steadily worsening
- Trouble walking, foot drop, or major balance problems

## 2-Week Safe Self-Care Plan

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

### Daily habits
- Stand up and walk **2–5 minutes every 30–45 minutes**
- Keep feet flat, hips and knees about 90 degrees, and screen at eye level
- Use a small **lumbar roll** or rolled towel behind the lower back
- Avoid long uninterrupted sitting, slouched couches, and wallet-in-pocket sitting
- Keep walking as tolerated; movement is usually better than bed rest

### Exercise plan, 3 times per week
- **Brisk walking**: 10–20 minutes
- **Cat-cow**: 8–10 slow reps
- **Pelvic tilts**: 10–12 reps
- **Glute bridges**: 2 sets of 8–12
- **Bird-dog**: 2 sets of 6–8 each side
- **Hip flexor stretch**: 20–30 seconds each side, 2 rounds
- **Hamstring stretch**: gentle, 20–30 seconds each side

Keep everything in a **mild discomfort range only**. Stop if pain becomes sharp, shoots down the leg, or clearly worsens afterward.

### Week-by-week focus
| Time | Focus | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| Days 1–3 | Reduce sitting load; add walking breaks | Pain settles after workday |
| Days 4–7 | Start gentle mobility + first strengthening session | Less stiffness after sitting |
| Days 8–10 | Repeat exercise session; improve workstation setup | Better tolerance for desk time |
| Days 11–14 | Continue walking and strengthening | Noticeable improvement in pain and function |

## Home-Care Items Within USD 80

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg

| Item | Typical use | Estimated cost |
|---|---|---|
| Lumbar support cushion or rolled towel | Improves sitting posture | USD 15–30 |
| Heating pad | Helps stiffness after work | USD 20–35 |
| Yoga mat | Makes floor exercises more comfortable | USD 15–25 |
| Resistance band | Useful for glute and core work | USD 10–20 |
| Timer or phone reminder | Prompts standing breaks | USD 0–10 |

A practical budget mix is: **lumbar support + heating pad + resistance band**, usually staying near or under **USD 80**.

## When to Reassess

If pain is **not improving after 2–4 weeks**, or if it keeps returning despite better sitting habits and exercise, a clinician or physical therapist can check for specific movement issues and tailor a plan.
